messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@novahealth.com>, Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: NovaHealth pilot - token econ spotcheck & requested inputs

Hi Lina / Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we draft the Mutual Action Plan for the pilot, wanted to surface a short spot-check on unit economics so we can lock the cost gate in the MAP milestone list. I've attached a working MAP workbook (NovaHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short sensitivity run showing batching/caching tradeoffs (batching-sensitivity-report.pdf).

Key assumptions we used in the workbook (please confirm or correct):
- Expected request profile: 9k requests/day in pilot week 1, ramping to ~45k r/day in steady-state pilot (QPS ~0.5 peak).
- Average tokens per request (input+output): baseline 420 tokens; 90thpct 1,100 tokens.
- Cacheable prefix rate: 28% (we assume user prompts include templated clinical forms where KV / prefix cache helps).
- KV cache hit efficiency: 75% on cacheable requests (reduces decoding compute).
- Batching target: dynamic batching up to 8 reqs per worker with latency SLO 250ms p95; for tighter latency use batch size 2-4.
- Model variant: open-llama-70B-quant (profiling uses quantized 4-bit path) with cost of $0.85 per 1M tokens in hosted plan equivalent for comparisons.

From these inputs, the workbook yields estimated cost per active user session of ~$0.032 (avg) and cost per 1k requests of ~$1.80. Those numbers shift ~+/-35% across the batching / cache sensitivity bounds.

Ask: can you confirm the expected daily request counts and give a quick estimate of the fraction of requests you expect to be fully templated (i.e., prefix + static fields that are cacheable)? That single number materially moves the MAP cost gate. Also confirm whether NovaHealth requires <200ms p95 (we heard 250ms in product) — that drives batch sizing choices.

I'll loop Ben and Karthik for ops and batching recommendations; want to get the MAP milestones updated to include a cost-validation checkpoint (pre-prod week) before any PO is issued.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm request counts and cacheable fraction by 2027-02-15.
- Redwood runs a 2-day stress run using your sample traffic (we'll produce an updated sensitivity table).
- MAP milestone: "Cost validation & acceptance" (sign-off threshold: 15% deviation from projected unit cost).

Thanks —
Monica
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: NovaHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx (workbook), batching-sensitivity-report.pdf (summary)
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@novahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@novahealth.com>, NovaHealth Procurement <procure@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: NovaHealth pilot - token econ spotcheck & requested inputs

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. Quick answers below to help you run the sensitivity:
- Expected pilot traffic: Week 1: 7.5k r/day; Week 2: 22k r/day; steady pilot peak: ~48k r/day (spiky: most load between 09:00-12:00 ET).
- Average tokens: from our telemetry sample: mean ~390 tokens, median 320, 95th 1,020.
- Cacheable fraction: roughly 34% of requests are template-driven (patient intake forms + repeat clinical questions).
- Latency requirement: product team would like <=200ms p95 if feasible; acceptance threshold is <=250ms p95. If you can't meet 200ms at the target cost, we'll discuss trade-offs.

Procurement looped in for timing: we aim to complete procurement and a pilot PO by end of March. Please include an estimate for a 30-day pilot with the ramp above in the workbook.

Happy to hop on a quick sync if you want to review assumptions live — Linda and I are available Wed morning our time.

Best,
Lina
Head of Product – NovaHealth

---
Note: attaching an internal traffic sample to procurement in a separate email.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: NovaHealth pilot - token econ spotcheck & requested inputs

Monica / Karthik —

Thanks, Lina — those numbers are helpful. A few operational clarifications and a short suggestion for the MAP wording so procurement has a clear acceptance criterion:

Operational clarifications (will update workbook after we validate):
- We'll model two serving profiles in the sensitivity sheet:
  1) Low-latency profile: target p95 <=200ms, batching capped at 3, KV-prefetch enabled; expected cost multiplier +28% vs baseline.
  2) Cost-optimized profile: p95 target <=250ms, batching up to 8, aggressive KV cache (where applicable); expected cost multiplier -18% vs baseline.
- Cache behavior: with 34% cacheable fraction and ~75% cache-hit efficiency, the effective token decode reduction is ~25% across requests. We'll show the math in the MAP workbook (sheet: "cache_model").
- Batching sensitivity: we simulated median latency vs batch sizes using your traffic sample; for your peak window we estimate batching size ~5 will hit p95 ~220ms on the quantized 70B path.

Suggested MAP language for the cost-validation milestone: "Pilot Cost Validation: Redwood will run a production-like 48-hour validation using NovaHealth sample traffic. If realized unit cost deviates by >15% from the MAP estimate under the chosen latency profile, parties will meet to re-scope pilot volume or select alternative model variant. Acceptance requires documented sign-off from NovaHealth Product and Procurement."

Can we add a MAP sub-milestone that records the chosen latency profile ("Low-latency" or "Cost-optimized") prior to the 48-hour run? That will make acceptance criteria deterministic.

I'll incorporate the updated sensitivity runs and push a refreshed MAP workbook by EOW.

Thanks —
Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Lina / Ethan / Procurement —

Appreciate the prompt responses. Attached is the updated MAP workbook (NovaHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx) and the batching sensitivity summary. Summary of what changed and explicit MAP additions: 

1) Inputs updated per NovaHealth telemetry: mean tokens 390, cacheable fraction 34%, pilot ramp updated (7.5k → 48k r/day).
2) Two latency profiles captured (Low-latency / Cost-optimized) with deterministic acceptance criteria.
3) New MAP sub-milestone: "Latency profile selection (Low-latency | Cost-optimized) — must be set before 48-hour validation run."
4) Cost-validation milestone language added (15% deviation threshold); acceptance requires sign-off from NovaHealth Product + Procurement.
5) Pilot estimate sheet: a 30-day pilot row with expected spend ranges, broken down by token, transient bandwidth, and burst capacity costs for dedicated pools if requested.

Ask / next steps:
- Please confirm chosen latency profile by Tue 2027-02-23 so we can schedule the 48-hour run for the first week of March.
- Procurement: if you have preferred contract language on cost overrun / PO cap for pilot, flag those clauses now; we'll route to Legal.
- I'll drop the finalized MAP into the HubSpot deal and attach the acceptance checklist. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NVH-2027-07

If we get profile selection and procurement feedback this week, we can keep the March PO target. Otherwise, we recommend shifting the run to mid-March to allow for procurement review.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the pilot.

Monica
